newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO stable to firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO stable to firmer.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Wednesday in stagnant, late trade, with low sulphurs still pressured by mild weather and cheap gas prices, while high sulphurs were buoyed by recent interest for Mexico.
"Overall, resid looks terrible. Gas is cheap and there's no demand, but high sulphur looks pretty good," said one cash trader, noting Mexico was still looking for HS barrels.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $16.25 a barrel, with July one percent paper done early at $16.25 and still quoted in the $16.25-50 area, also steady, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again notionally eased by 25 cents to $16.50-75.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to higher, with three percent inching up to $14.50-75.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $16.00-25, while three percent gained slightly to about $14.50.
USG July three percent paper was still pegged at about $14.50 despite softer crude.

A Florida utility issued a tender with four options for delivery by July 15 as follows: 100,000 barrels of two pct; or 100,000 barrels of two pct and 75,000 barrels of 1.8 pct; or up to 180,000 barrels of 1.8 pct; or up to 230,000 barrels of 2.5 pct. Bids are due on Thursday at 1000 EDT.

New York city gate gas prices firmed a few cents Wednesday to about the $2.40/mmBtu level, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained more than five cents to about $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
